list.title: Encryption Keys
list.sectionIntro: AES encryption keys protecting sensitive data at rest. Rotate periodically for compliance.
list.headerTooltipLifecycle: Derived from tracked ciphertext targets and migration batch state. See key detail for full snapshot.
list.headerTooltipStatus: Primary = used for new encryption; Enabled = decryption only; Disabled = retired.
list.headerTooltipRecords: Prefix scan across the same targets as re-encryption batches. PRIMARY: current ciphertext volume on this key (sanity check / trend). ENABLED: migration backlog still encrypted with this key. Em dash for PENDING and DISABLED.
list.headerTooltipPrimarySince: Date this key was promoted to primary.
list.reencryptButtonTooltip: Migrate records encrypted with this key to the current primary key.

help.sectionContent: AES-256 encryption keys protecting sensitive data at rest. The PRIMARY key encrypts new data. Old keys remain ENABLED until all their records are re-encrypted. The Tracked column shows prefix-based ciphertext counts: for the primary key it reflects live volume (useful to spot unexpected growth); for enabled keys it is the migration backlog.

keyStatus.helpPrimary: Active key used for all new encryption operations.
keyStatus.helpEnabled: Key can decrypt existing data but is not used for new encryption.
keyStatus.helpDisabled: Key is retired; all data has been re-encrypted to a newer key.
keyStatus.helpPending: Key created but not yet promoted or in use.

stageHelp.ENABLED_IN_USE: Old key: ciphertext or migration work may remain.
stageHelp.DRAINED: No tracked ciphertext rows and no incomplete migration batches for this key.

keyDetail.title: Key #{{id}}
keyDetail.reencryptionWallClockTooltip: Parallel-aware estimate from completed batch timestamps: the longest shard in each shard group, plus the duration of other completed batches. Available once the key is fully drained.

reencryptDialog.title: Re-encrypt Key #{{id}}
reencryptDialog.warning: This will create and process re-encryption batches to migrate all records from key #{{id}} to the current primary key. This may take time depending on the number of records.
reencryptDialog.toastAccepted: Re-encryption accepted for key #{{id}} — watch the batches table

batchStatus.helpFailed: Re-encryption failed; use Resume to retry.
batchStatus.helpPaused: Batch paused; use Resume to continue.

batchesSection.title: Re-encryption Batches
batchesSection.sectionHelpContent: Each row is one migration job: a table column still encrypted with an old key is moved to the current PRIMARY. Create batches only inserts queue rows (no crypto yet)—the scheduler or Trigger full processes them. Resume runs processBatch for that row.
batchesSection.sectionHelpFilters: Optional filters apply on the server. Table and Column are exact matches on database identifiers. Old key and New key use the same numeric IDs as the keys list above—they are Tink keyset IDs (not an arbitrary sequential counter). Enter an exact ID to narrow batches to a specific source or destination key; there is no meaningful “range” search on these values.
batchesSection.helpCreateBatches: Creates batch rows for every applicable old key and encrypted column. Does not re-encrypt data—use for the next scheduled run or inspection.
batchesSection.helpTriggerFull: Creates missing batches, then processes all pending and resumable batches immediately (heavy—use for tests or emergencies).
batchesSection.helpResume: Runs processing for this batch (pending or failed). Same as POST …/reencryption-batches/{id}/resume.
batchesSection.tooltipTargetTable: Exact database table name for this batch (e.g. ezkey_enrollment). Server-side exact match.
batchesSection.tooltipTargetColumn: Exact column name holding encrypted data in that table.
batchesSection.tooltipOldKeyId: Source key: numeric ID from the keys table (Tink key id). Exact match filter—not a range.
batchesSection.tooltipNewKeyId: Destination key: numeric ID from the keys table (Tink key id), usually the current PRIMARY. Exact match.
batchesSection.emptyFiltered: No batches match the selected filter.
batchesSection.tooltipPerf: Wall time between start and completion; rate is records done divided by that duration.

rotateDialog.title: Rotate Encryption Key
rotateDialog.warning: This will generate a new AES encryption key and promote it as the primary. A background re-encryption job will start to migrate existing records.
